title: DROIDFUZZ: Proprietary Driver Fuzzing for Embedded Android Devices
problem: Embedded Android devices (smart home, automotive, IoT) require security validation, but traditional kernel testing cannot reach vendor-specific driver logic in the Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL). Proprietary drivers are black-boxes; standard fuzzing frameworks cannot effectively probe HAL/kernel boundaries.
motivation: Security-critical embedded Android deployments need vulnerability detection in proprietary driver implementations; HAL-level bugs are common but under-tested.
method: DroidFuzz finds security bugs in proprietary device drivers by testing them at the boundary between hardware drivers and the operating system. It first explores which driver interfaces exist on the device, then generates test inputs that are valid on both sides of this boundary. Rather than using random data, it watches how the code behaves during testing and uses that feedback to probe deeper into driver logic.
key_novelty: The key idea is testing vendor-specific drivers and the operating system together at their boundary by generating test inputs that work on both sides, guided by how the code actually executes.
contributions: DroidFuzz fuzzer for vendor-specific Android driver testing
Pre-testing HAL driver probing for interface identification
Kernel-user relational payload generation for valid cross-boundary inputs
Cross-boundary execution state feedback for guided fuzzing
12 previously unknown security-critical bugs found in 7 embedded Android devices; all confirmed by vendors
limitations: Evaluation limited to 7 devices; generalization to diverse HAL implementations; zero-day exploitability assessment; comparison with other HAL-aware fuzzing tools not provided.
primary_theme: cross-layer fuzzing for vendor-specific Android driver vulnerability discovery
